ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
In the process of moving a negative point charge with a charge of $3\times{10}^{-8}\mathrm{C}$ from point A to point B in an electrostatic field, the work done by the electrostatic force is $1.5 \times{10}^{-7}\mathrm{J}$; in the process of moving the point charge from point B to point C, the work done against the electrostatic force is $9\times{10}^{-8}\mathrm{J}$.

1. From this, we can determine the potential difference between points A and C in the electric field.

ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: In the process of moving a negative point charge of $3\times10^{-8}\,\mathrm{C}$ from point A to point B in an electrostatic field, the work done by the electrostatic force is $1.5\times10^{-7}\,\mathrm{J}$; in the process of moving the point charge from point B to point C, the work done against the electrostatic force is $9\times10^{-8}\,\mathrm{J}$. From this, determine the potential difference between points A and C in the electric field.
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Given charge q = -3×10^-8 C. For A→B, the work done by the electrostatic force is W_AB = +1.5×10^-7 J. For B→C, “work done against the electrostatic force” is 9×10^-8 J, so the work done by the electrostatic force is W_BC = -9×10^-8 J. Treating A→B→C as one path, the total electrostatic work is W_AC = W_AB + W_BC = 1.5×10^-7 - 9×10^-8 = 6×10^-8 J. Using W_AC = q(V_A - V_C), we get V_A - V_C = W_AC/q = (6×10^-8)/(-3×10^-8) = -2 V.
